name: Doge's Palace
overview: The Doge's Palace (Palazzo Ducale) was the residence of the Doge of Venice and the seat of Venetian government for centuries. This masterpiece of Gothic architecture houses spectacular artwork and connects to the famous Bridge of Sighs.
history: This pink palace was the seat of power for the Venetian Republic for over 1,000 years (697-1797), where 120 Doges ruled over a maritime empire stretching from Northern Italy to Constantinople! The palace witnessed incredible intrigue: Doges were elected for life but lived under constant surveillance, unable to leave Venice or even read private letters without permission. The famous Bridge of Sighs earned its romantic name from Lord Byron, but it was actually the last view of beautiful Venice that prisoners saw before entering the dungeons - hence the 'sighs.' The palace's Golden Staircase was where foreign ambassadors climbed to meet the Doge, deliberately designed to intimidate with its opulence. In the Great Council Hall, Tintoretto's massive painting 'Paradise' (the world's largest oil painting) took 6 years to complete. The palace also housed Europe's first state-sponsored spy network and the feared Council of Ten, who could condemn anyone to death or exile. Secret denunciation boxes around the city allowed anonymous accusations! After Napoleon conquered Venice in 1797, ending the Republic, the palace became a museum, preserving the memory of La Serenissima - 'The Most Serene Republic.'
highlights: Bridge of Sighs connecting to the prison
Golden Staircase (Scala d'Oro) with Tintoretto frescoes
Grand Council Chamber with Tintoretto's Paradise
Secret Itineraries tour through hidden chambers and prisons
tips: Book skip-the-line tickets online. The Secret Itineraries tour requires advance booking and offers fascinating insights. Photography is not allowed inside most rooms. Allow 2-3 hours for a complete visit.
